title: 4D viewer scene sidecar
description: The scene.json the 4D viewer page reads. It exists so that the numbers the page prints -- the cone, the counts, whether the fixed pose was verified, whether the scene was truncated to fit a budget -- are validated data rather than strings assembled in a template. Everything here is also recoverable from the .g4d header; the sidecar is what lets a page state it before the binary has finished downloading.

file.description: The .g4d beside this file, or null when the page has it inlined.

dynamic_count.description: Gaussians bound to the deformation scaffold. They come first in the file.

chunk_bytes.description: Bytes per .g4d chunk, so a page can say what the motion actually cost.

azimuth_deg.description: Half-angle. The camera is hard clamped to this, and it is measured from the solved arc cameras rather than asserted.

source.description: Where the half-angles came from. Anything other than measured means the number is weaker than it looks, and the page says so.

verified means the pose was confirmed against masked hold keyframes. asserted means registration failed and the pose was inherited from the rest-window cameras without confirmation -- which the viewer must surface, not bury.

loop.description: A one-to-three second clip is not cyclic, so a forward loop cuts visibly. ping-pong is the honest default and the transport says which is on.

rate.description: Initial playback rate. Below one by default because a one-second clip at 1x is over before a user finishes a single camera drag.

truncated.description: The export dropped gaussians to fit a budget. If true the page must say so: the scene on screen is not the scene that was trained.

caveat.description: One sentence about what lies outside the cone. Required in spirit: the page prints it verbatim.

evaluation.description: Any quality number carried here is temporal hold-out only -- it measures motion interpolation between observed frames, never novel-view synthesis, because a fixed camera has no held-out view to score.
